messages.subject: Adding a geom_vline layer
parts:
I would like to add vlines to a plot with mutliple line plots. I'd be
using a different data frame for the data. I'd also like the vline to
show up in the legend.

I must be missing something simple because I can't get

For example:


#make a simple pyramid shape
yv <- c( seq(1,100), seq( 101,1))
xv <- seq(-1200,-1000)
lv <- c("series1")
test.df <- as.data.frame( yv )
test.df$xv <- xv
test.df$lv <- lv
#make the plot
pl.test <- qplot(xv, yv, data= test.df , geom=c ("line"),
colour=lv)
pl.test + scale_x_continuous ( breaks =c(-1100 ) , limits=c
(-1150, -1050))

#put a value for the vline in a df
ext.mean <- c( -1105.4)
test.df.vline <- as.data.frame( ext.mean )
test.df.vline$col <- c("other mean")
pl.test + geom_vline ( aes( intercept = ext.mean ), data =
test.df.vline, stat="identity")
# pl.test <- qplot(ext.mean, data= test.df.vline )
pl.test

Thanks so much!
Keith

messages.subject: Re: Adding a geom_vline layer
parts:
In reading more of Mr. Wickham's  thesis, I see that qplot is not the correct choice when using different data frames in different layers.  So, now I see how this works better:


#make a simple pyradmid shape

yv <- c( seq(1,100), seq( 101,1))
xv <-  seq(-1200,-1000)
lv <- c("series1")
test.df <- as.data.frame( yv )
test.df$xv <- xv
test.df$lv <- lv

#put a value for the vline in a df
ext.mean <- c( -1105.4)
test.df.vline <- as.data.frame( ext.mean  )
test.df.vline$col <- c("other mean")

test.df.vline$zer <- c(0)

pl.test <- ggplot( ) +
  layer(data=test.df.vline, mapping=aes(color = col, x=ext.mean, y=zer, xend = ext.mean,), geom="vline", stat="identity", position="identity") +
  layer( data=test.df, mapping =aes (x=xv, y=yv, color=lv), geom="line")
pl.test


I'm now investigating how to change the legend symbols for each color item... if that makes sense.

Keith

Well sorry if I wasted your time with this issue.  I'm getting close to what I was hoping for.  I'll post the sample chart and the code that made it, in case it might help someone else.

The chart has a geom_line, and geom_vline, and a geom_rect (all using different data frames.)   I'm not sure about the xend parameter for the vline layer.  May not be necessary, but I saw an error when it was absent that led me to add it.

#make a simple pyradmid shape
yv <- c( seq(1,100), seq( 101,1))
xv <-  seq(-1200,-1000)
lv <- c("series1")
test.df <- as.data.frame( yv )
test.df$xv <- xv
test.df$lv <- lv

#put a value for the vline in a df
ext.mean <- c( -1105.4)
test.df.vline <- as.data.frame( ext.mean  )
test.df.vline$col <- c("other mean")
test.df.vline$zer <- c(0)

#make a data frame for a rectangle
xmin <- c( -1111.4)
test.df.rect <- as.data.frame( xmin  )
test.df.rect$xmax <- c( -1058.2)
test.df.rect$ymin <- c( 0)
test.df.rect$ymax <- c( 100)
test.df.rect$col <- c( "other s.d.")

pl.test <- ggplot( )+
     scale_fill_manual (name="Fill",  values=c( alpha("tan", 0.2))  ) + scale_colour_brewer (name="Legend"  ) +
  layer( data=test.df, mapping =aes (x=xv, y=yv, color=lv), geom="line") +
  layer( data=test.df.rect, mapping=aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin=ymin, ymax=ymax,  fill=col  ), geom="rect")  +
layer(data=test.df.vline, mapping=aes(color = col, x=ext.mean, y=zer, xend = ext.mean,), geom="vline", stat="identity", position="identity")
pl.test <- pl.test +  scale_x_continuous (  breaks =c(-1100) , limits=c(-1150, -1050))
pl.test

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Adding a geom_vline layer
parts:
Hi Keith,

You should be using xintercept with geom_vline:

ggplot() +
geom_line(aes(x = xv, y = yv, color = lv), test.df) +
geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill=col),
test.df.rect) +
geom_vline(aes(color = col, xintercept=ext.mean), test.df.vline) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks = -1100, limits = c(-1150, -1050)) +
scale_fill_manual(name="Fill", values = alpha("tan", 0.2)) +
scale_colour_brewer(name="Legend")

I really recommend using the geom functions rather than the more
general layer function because you can more easily scan the start of
each line to see what it's doing.

Hadley
